_: WHERE EVERY ANDROID SIGNING FINGERPRINT COMES FROM. This file is NEVER
deployed: it lives beside site/, not inside it. assetlinks.json is parsed
by Android and holds nothing but canonical Digital Asset Links; the notes
that make it governable are here, and tests/doctrine-app-links.js is what
ties the two together.
A fingerprint may appear in assetlinks.json only if it appears here with
status `vouched`. `awaited` is a slot declared before its key exists.
`unattributed` is a value nobody can trace, and it is refused from
assetlinks.json by name.
kind: debug | release | store. A debug key and a publication key may not
be SERVED from assetlinks.json at the same time -- the gate enforces
that, so the question is put on the day it becomes real rather than the
day someone remembers.
THAT RULE USED TO READ THIS FILE INSTEAD OF THE DEPLOYMENT, AND ON 17
AUGUST 2026 IT DEADLOCKED. Vouching the publication key below -- an act
of pure record-keeping, changing nothing any device can reach -- fired
tests/doctrine-app-links.js, while scripts/check-apk-signing.sh refuses
any state in which debug-local is NOT vouched, because the debug lane of
apk.yml holds the certificate it reads off its artefact against that
entry. No state of this file satisfied both; all three were applied to a
copy that day and all three failed.
Neither gate was weakened. The rule was asking the wrong question: the
harm its own comment named was a debug key in a production
assetlinks.json, and the condition it evaluated was a debug key in this
ledger. `vouched` here means somebody wrote down which key a value comes
from and how to recompute it -- a PRECONDITION of serving, as the
paragraph above says, and not the act of it. Since 17 August 2026 the
rule reads what assetlinks.json serves, and it fires on the day the
publication fingerprint is served alongside the debug one, which is what
publishing to any device that carries nothing yet requires.
THE DECISION IS STILL UNMADE, and it is now attached to the day it
matters instead of to this file's redness: see debug-local's
withdraw_when, and .superpowers/sdd/2026-08-17-publication/
task-M-report.md for what each way out costs.

fingerprints.name: debug-local
fingerprints.origin: The debug keystore committed at packages/app/android/app/debug.keystore, which is what `signingConfigs.debug` names and therefore what every device build of this repository is signed with. It was a per-machine ~/.android/debug.keystore until 2026-09-06, which was wrong twice over: the value differed on every developer's laptop, and it was not the key the application actually carried -- installing a build over another failed with INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE, which is how it was found.
fingerprints.reproduce: keytool -list -v -keystore packages/app/android/app/debug.keystore -storepass android -alias androiddebugkey | grep SHA256:
fingerprints.withdraw_when: NOT YET, AND NOT WHEN A PUBLICATION KEY MERELY EXISTS -- one has existed since 8 August 2026 and is vouched below. What this key protects is still load-bearing: the APK the maintainer hands his friend is signed with it, and so is the demonstration Pixel, which AGENTS.md §7.2 freezes on that signature and forbids uninstalling. Taking 4B:19:FF:28:... out of assetlinks.json would stop https://messagr.eu/i/<token> from opening the application on the only two phones that carry it, which is the entry path to the product; and no publication build can replace those installs, because Android refuses an update signed by another key and the uninstall that would be needed erases the account, the Megolm keys and the history of 11 August. THE CONDITION IS THE FIELD, NOT THE KEYRING: it goes when no install signed by it is still in use -- when the friend's phone has been migrated to a publication build and the Pixel has been retired or exempted by a decision that says so in writing. The publication lane added to apk.yml on 17 August 2026 makes that migration POSSIBLE for a device carrying nothing yet; it does not perform it, and it cannot perform it for these two. Until then this key stays vouched and stays served, and doctrine-app-links.js will refuse the day the publication fingerprint joins it in assetlinks.json -- which is the day this decision has to be made rather than described. task-M-report.md holds the proposal and what each way out costs.

fingerprints.name: release
fingerprints.origin: The maintainer's publication keystore, the one ~/.messagr-signature/identifiants.env names in MAGASIN: self-signed CN=Messagr, O=Messagr, C=FR, a 4096-bit RSA key signed SHA384withRSA, created 8 August 2026 and valid until 24 December 2053. It is the key a release is signed with -- `releaseKeystorePath` in android/app/build.gradle.kts and the three settings beside it name it from outside the repository, and `requireReleaseSigningMaterial` refuses to package a release without all four. THIS IS THE VALUE messagr.eu SERVED FROM 9 AUGUST 2026, and it sat in this registry as `unattributed-2026-08-09` for eight days for one reason: the task that wrote the registry searched its own worktree, found nothing but ~/.android/debug.keystore, and concluded that nothing here reproduced the value. The keystore was two directories outside that worktree and nobody looked there. The dates agree with the attribution -- the keystore is of 8 August 2026 and commit 385d26b imported the value on 9 August. Measured on 17 August 2026 with the command below and compared character for character against what site/.well-known/assetlinks.json served until 16 August 2026.
fingerprints.reproduce: . ~/.messagr-signature/identifiants.env && keytool -list -v -keystore "$MAGASIN" -alias "$ALIAS" -storepass "$MOT_DE_PASSE" | grep 'SHA256'  --  that file holds the keystore path, the alias and the password, and it is named here BY PATH AND NEVER BY CONTENT. A path is not a secret and is useful only to somebody already on this machine; refusing to name it would protect nothing and would cost the reproducibility this registry exists for.
fingerprints.withdraw_when: Never, as long as the application is published. This is the identity a store checks the upload against, and a copy already installed will not accept an update signed by anything else. If Play App Signing is turned on it stops being the certificate that reaches devices -- play-app-signing below is then the one that does -- but it stays the upload key and it stays here.

fingerprints.name: play-app-signing
fingerprints.origin: The certificate Google Play generates when Play App Signing re-signs the upload. THIS IS THE ONE THAT ACTUALLY REACHES DEVICES once the application is distributed by Play: the upload key above signs what is sent to Google, and Google signs what users install. An assetlinks.json carrying only the upload key verifies for no installed application at all, which is a failure that appears only after publication.
fingerprints.reproduce: Play Console, the application, Test and release, Setup, App signing: copy the SHA-256 shown under 'App signing key certificate'. Play also publishes a ready-made statement file on the same page.
fingerprints.withdraw_when: The application leaves Play, or Play App Signing is turned off -- which cannot be undone once enabled.
